_comment: doc 11 §2.15 (audio is doc 11's, Phase 2). The single tunables file for game/audio/: buses, the voice pool, every cue, the sim-event → cue rules, and the ambience beds. Nothing in game/audio/*.gd hardcodes a level, a cooldown or a distance (constitution §3): AudioEvents decides WHICH cue and WHEN from this file, AudioService only plays what it is handed. Streams resolve as `asset_root + <stream> + .wav`, all generated by tools/gen_audio.py.

mix._comment: `settings_key` is the ui/settings_model.gd row that scales the whole mix (data/ui.json.settings.rows: `sound_volume`, 0..1, default 0.8). At or below `silence_below_volume01` the Master bus is muted outright rather than played at -60 dB.
mix._comment_count_gain: Audio-2 ruling: a citywide blackout is LOUDER than one dark block. A rule that dedups by cue folds N events into one cue and carries the fold's `count`; `count_gain` turns that count into dB, `per_doubling_db` at a time, capped. A rule opts in with `"count_gain": true` (this default) or with its own object. `max_db` is the ruling's ceiling and tests/test_audio_model.gd holds it to +4 dB — twelve dark blocks is 3.58 doublings ≙ 5.7 dB uncapped, so the cap is what is actually doing the work, and that is the point: the difference between one block and the city is legible, and no fold can ever run away.
mix._comment_muffle: Interior muffle (doc 12 sheets/panels). When a sheet or panel covers more than `threshold01` of the screen the player is INSIDE something, and the city should be heard through it: an AudioEffectLowPassFilter on the Ambient bus alone, sliding from `open_hz` to `covered_hz` and trimming `covered_db`. The SFX and UI buses are untouched — a confirmation blip is in the room with the player, not out of the window. `ramp_s` is longer than the sheet's own animation so the mix settles after the panel rather than racing it.

pool._comment: One AudioStreamPlayer per voice, allocated once at setup. `max_per_cue` is what stops a storm from spending the whole pool on thunder; stealing prefers the oldest voice of the lowest priority.

world._comment: Positional model. The listener is the camera (the shell passes it in). `tile_m` matches constitution §6. `speed_of_sound_ms` is what delays thunder behind its flash (doc 11 §2.15). `position_keys` maps a payload id to a locator kind so the shell's `Callable(kind, id) -> Vector3` can place an event that only carries an id.
world._curves: `inverse` is ref_m/d with a linear window fade to exactly 0 at max_m (so a far event is dropped, not mixed at -60 dB); `linear` is the window alone; `none` opts a cue out of distance entirely — the player's own confirmation and a critical sting are feedback, not scenery.

sirens._comment: MOVING sirens (Audio-2 ruling; doc 11 §2.15 listed `vehicle_state.siren` as not-wired precisely because it needed this). Doc 10's feed is ~1,400 events per game hour, so the deliverable is the THROTTLE, not the emitter: at most `max_sources` sirens are ever audible, chosen nearest-first, and the choice is sticky so a unit does not pop in and out while two vehicles trade places a metre at a time. The doppler stays baked into `siren_pass` — nothing here pitch-shifts anything; a moving unit simply re-triggers its pass AT ITS CURRENT POSITION every `retrigger_s`, so distance and direction come out of the ordinary attenuation.
sirens._hysteresis: Three separate mechanisms, because a single radius pops three different ways. (1) `enter_m` < `exit_m`: a source has to come closer to win a slot than it has to stay to keep one. (2) `takeover_margin_m`: a waiting source only displaces an audible one when it is that many metres CLOSER, so two units running the same street never trade the slot back and forth. (3) `min_hold_s`: once a source is audible it keeps its slot for at least this long no matter what, which bounds how often the audible set can change at all.
sirens._comment_statuses: doc 06 §2.11's fleet FSM: a unit RESPONDING is running hot. ON_SCENE keeps its lightbar (doc 11 §2.12) but not its siren — a parked engine at a fire is not wailing — and RETURNING goes quiet. This list is the only place audio names a doc 06 status.

cues._comment: gain_db is the trim on top of the level already authored into the WAV. `pitch_jitter` is ± a fraction, drawn from the audio RNG stream, so a repeated cue never phases against itself. `duck` (0..1) pulls the ambience beds down while the cue lands.
cues._comment_cash: The payday. It sits on the UI bus rather than SFX and it is never attenuated (see the two rules below), because money arriving is FEEDBACK — the player's own tap paid, or a crew they never watched leave came back with a bounty — and feedback that gets quieter because the camera drifted is feedback the player stops trusting. Its priority sits above `purchase` for the same reason: a coin landing must not be the voice the pool steals when a storm is on.

events._comment: First matching rule wins (AlertsModel's rule shape, same reasons). `match` is exact equality, `range` is min/max on a number; both may read a derived field — `@distance_m` is the metres from the listener to the event, resolved before any rule is tried, which is what lets thunder pick crack-vs-rumble without a second concept. `dedup_by` is `cue` (all of them are one story: twelve dark blocks are ONE thunk) or `key` (each entity is its own). `cooldown_s` is measured from the last accepted request of that identity, not from playback, so a delayed cue still gates the next one.

A pump, tank or treatment works is a doc-02 building that announces itself on doc 05's own event (`cmd_place_water_component` step 1), so it was in OBSERVED_TYPES for the crane loop and in nothing else -- the most expensive purchase in the curriculum was the one purchase in the game that made no sound. Same cue, same key, same numbers as the row above, because it is the same beat: the player spent money and a footprint appeared.

Power. BlockDarkChanged is the sim's truth; render_blackout_started / render_relight_started are doc 11 §2.15's renderer hooks for the same beat. Both are mapped on purpose — they share a cue identity, so a shell that feeds both event sources still gets exactly one thunk per blackout.

events._comment_count_gain: These four are exactly what `count_gain` was ruled for: the fold is the whole point of the cue, and its `count` is how much of the city just went dark. One block is the authored level; the cap lands at eight blocks and never moves again.

events._comment: Lightning. `speed_of_sound` turns the metres into the delay behind the flash; the near rule fires the crack, everything further away smears into the rumble. Both carry world_pos already, so no locator is involved.
Incidents. doc 08's notification class decides the sting: P1 critical gets the urgent one, everything else the routine one.

Dispatch — the DEPARTURE beat. unit_dispatched carries no position, so the incident's tile (remembered from incident_created) places it; the pass-by fade and the doppler are authored into the asset, and distance only sets the level. Everything after the departure belongs to the `sirens` throttle above, which takes over at the unit's real position: `key_prefix` puts this rule on the throttle's own identity (`siren_pass/u7`), so the two can never sound the same unit twice at the station door.

The payday, Wave 14. Two doors, ONE identity. `ui_cash` is the shell's synthetic cue on a street collect the player tapped for (the same door `ui_confirm` uses, `AudioService.UI_CASH`); `incident_resolved` with a reward on it is the bounty a dispatch earned while the player was somewhere else entirely — that payload has carried `reward` since doc 06 shipped and NOTHING has ever sounded it, which is the audible half of why an automatic dispatch felt like it paid nothing. Both resolve to `cash`, they dedup and cool down on that shared identity, and the 0.35 s cooldown is deliberately longer than a sim tick: a collect whose command lands a tick after the tap can therefore never double-strike, and a player sweeping up four dogs in a second hears four coins at the rate an ear can count them, not a machine gun.

The payday BACKWARDS, Wave 17 (doc 12 §2.22). Rushing a project is money leaving, so it takes `purchase` — the deck's spend cue, the one `building_placed_sim` already uses — and not `cash`: a player who hears a till when their balance DROPS learns the wrong thing about their own treasury, and that is the one thing the coin was added to teach. It is never attenuated, for §2.21's reason: this is feedback on the player's own thumb, and feedback that gets quieter because the camera drifted is feedback they stop trusting. The completion the rush causes is NOT sounded here — it arrives a moment later on `building_completed` and rings `construct_complete`, exactly as an unrushed one does, which is the whole point of a rush firing the same events a natural finish fires.

beds._comment: Looping ambience. `source` names the computation in AudioEvents: `day`/`night` cross-fade on the shell's night01, `precip` follows weather_changed.precip01, `wind` maps wind_kph into 0..1, `storm` is the two of them together, `sites` follows how many construction sites are live and how far the nearest one is. Each bed's gain is lerped over mix.bed_ramp_s and the player is stopped outright below mix.bed_stop_below, so a silent bed costs nothing.
beds._comment_storm: The storm bed goes UNDER the wind bed, never instead of it: `storm_wind` is sub-100 Hz buffet, roar and rattle, and the wind bed is still what carries the gusting mid. It needs BOTH inputs — `min_kph` for wind and `min_precip01` for rain — because a dry gale is a gale and a still downpour is a downpour, and only the two together are a storm. `precip_weight` is how much of the level rain is allowed to carry once the wind gate is open. It comes up on `exponent` 1.6 so a merely blustery afternoon stays under it.
